name: AppShell
usage: The root of an application: top bar, sidebar navigation and the page

props.name: header
props.description:
Content of the top bar, laid out in a row with step 3 gaps: usually AppShell.Toggle, the name of the
application, a Spacer, then search and the account menu. Rendered in a `header` landmark.

props.name: sidebar
props.description: Content of the sidebar, usually a Nav; it scrolls on its own. A Nav inside follows the collapsed state.

props.name: children
props.description: The page, rendered in the `main` landmark, which scrolls on its own; usually a Page.

props.name: collapsed
props.description:
Collapsed sidebar (controlled): icons only. Applies to wide layouts; on narrow ones, the sidebar is a drawer
that is closed until AppShell.Toggle opens it.

props.name: onCollapsedChange
props.description: Called with the new state when AppShell.Toggle collapses or expands the sidebar of a wide layout.

props.name: rail
props.description:
What the collapsed sidebar shows: an icon rail (the Nav inside shows icons only, with tooltips), or nothing
with `rail={false}`, for navigation without icons such as documentation.

props.name: sidebarWidth
props.description: Width step of the expanded sidebar: `sm` 240, `md` 280, `lg` 320 px (the widths of SplitView).

props.name: flush
props.description: Main area without padding, for full-screen interfaces (a chat, image viewing) whose root is a flush SplitView.

props.name: contained
props.description: Fills its container instead of the viewport: for an application inside a frame, a preview or an example.

props.name: mainId
props.description: `id` of the `main` element, the target of the skip link; generated when omitted.

members.name: AppShell.Toggle
members.summary:
The button that shows or hides the sidebar, to place in the header (usually first) or anywhere inside
AppShell: on wide layouts it collapses and expands the sidebar ("Collapse sidebar" / "Expand sidebar"), on
narrow ones it opens the sidebar drawer ("Open navigation"). It is an IconButton with `aria-expanded` and
`aria-controls`; outside AppShell it renders nothing.

examples.name: Basic
examples.title: Basic usage
examples.description:
The header holds AppShell.Toggle, the name of the application and the account; the sidebar holds a Nav; the
page goes in the children. The sidebar collapses to icons with the toggle, and becomes a drawer when the frame
is narrower than 960 px. `contained` keeps the example inside this page: an application leaves it out, so that
the frame fills the window.

examples.name: FullScreen
examples.title: Full-screen interface
examples.description: `flush` removes the padding of the main area, for interfaces whose root is a flush SplitView, such as a chat.

examples.name: Controlled
examples.title: Controlled collapse with a shortcut
examples.description:
Keep `collapsed` in your state to save it or to change it from elsewhere, such as with the `[` key. AppShell.Toggle
calls `onCollapsedChange`.
